prompt:
Today is 2026-10-23. You are connected to the Prism MCP server.

Build a geo-intelligence dashboard on AIR POLLUTION for an environmental policy team in India, using the
Prism tools. They want to see, on one screen and then below it, where the issue is being reported, where it is
studied, how India compares with the world, and which places and stories are driving it.

Panels:
1. Header KPI tiles: total coverage, India's share of placed coverage and its lift, how much coverage could be
   placed at all, and the research volume. Each tile states its window.
2. World map: the country each article is about, coloured by lift over the all-news baseline, with a ranked table
   (articles, share, lift).
3. India state map: coverage and lift by state. The state level returns places outside India too; show only
   Indian states on the map and list what you excluded.
4. City leaderboard: the Indian cities and the NCR cluster, with lift.
5. Trend: monthly coverage for India against the rest of the world, with the incomplete newest month handled.
6. Studied vs reported vs patented: the separate geography lanes for research and patents next to news, never
   added together, with India and three comparators.
7. The critical stories: date, publisher, headline and link.
8. Data quality: placement share, windows and censoring, and any artefacts you caught (labels that are not
   places, acronym collisions), so a reader trusts the map for the right reasons.


HOW TO BUILD IT
- One self-contained HTML document inside a single ```html fenced block, nothing outside it.
- Charts: Vega-Lite 5 from cdn.jsdelivr.net (vega@5.30.0, vega-lite@5.21.0, vega-embed@6.26.0), each drawn with
  vegaEmbed('#<id>', spec) into an element with that id, with a pixel width (never "container") and the data inline.
- Maps: world countries from the relative URL world_india_official.geojson (properties.iso3, properties.name);
  Indian states from india_states_official.geojson (properties.name, and properties.key = the lower-case state
  label Prism returns, e.g. "delhi", "uttar pradesh"). Both draw India with its official outline. Use no other map file.
- Every number on the page names the Prism call it came from (a small source line under each panel is enough)
  and the window it was counted over. If a call returned nothing or a row is an artefact, say so on the page.
- Light and dark readable, works at phone width, a CSV download button for each table (built from the embedded data).
- Before you answer, run check_report on the finished page and fix everything it lists.

args.html:
Air pollution — where it is reported, studied and patented

Built 2026-10-23 from Prism MCP. News windows end at the ingest-safe cutoff (2026-06-01, exclusive); geography labels end at the enrichment bound (2026-05-01, exclusive). All index partition passed strict reads (system.status). The article store (system.article_store) refused connections at build time. The critical-story feed still resolved 7 records; 3 more ids did not resolve.

1 · Headline numbers

Total coverage28,212articles mentioning "air pollution", Jun 2024 – May 2026 · 23,291 of them priority 7+ ("critical") · src: news.resolve / news.trends
India share · lift31.2% · 4.7×9,245 articles placed in India = 31.2% of country placements (59.3% of the 15,590 placed articles, since one article can carry several countries); lift 4.7× vs all-news baseline · May 2024 – Apr 2026 · src: news.geography (country)
Coverage placed at all54.9%15,590 of 28,420 matched articles carry a country · state 50.2%, city 47.0% · May 2024 – Apr 2026 · src: news.geography
Research volume82,768typed papers 2017–2025 (title + keywords, audited phrasings) · 36,149 with "air pollution" in the title alone · src: research.browse / analysis.history

2 · Which country the coverage is about (lift over the all-news baseline)

Grey = not in the top 25 returned, which does not mean zero. Colour scale is log lift; 1× = the same share as news in general. Src: news.geography level=country, 2024-05-01 – 2026-05-01 (exclusive), placed 54.9%.

3 · Indian states

Src: news.geography level=state, 2024-05-01 – 2026-05-01 (exclusive), placed 50.2%. Lift colour on a log scale; grey = not returned in the top 40.

Excluded from the map (state level returns places outside India): .
Not a state: "national capital region" (396, lift 74.3×) is a planning region spanning Delhi, Haryana, UP and Rajasthan, so it appears in panel 4. "centre" (636, lift 16.1×) is not a place; it is almost certainly "the Centre", meaning India's union government. Ambiguous: "punjab" (790) could be the Indian or the Pakistani province. It is mapped to India and flagged.

4 · City leaderboard — Indian cities and the NCR cluster

Src: news.geography level=city, 2024-05-01 – 2026-05-01 (exclusive), placed 47.0%. Bars = articles; label = lift. NCR rows are tinted. NCR counts overlap and are not summed.

Artefacts caught: "sirsa" (253, lift 271.6×) is very likely the surname of Delhi's environment minister, Manjinder Singh Sirsa, rather than the town of Sirsa in Haryana. It is kept but flagged. "delhi" has exactly 6,213 at both state and city level, so it is one label resolved twice. Labels returned as cities that are not cities, and are excluded: congress (728), earth (379), winter (158), california (766). Non-Indian cities excluded: .

5 · Monthly coverage: India vs everything else

Src: news.trends (all) and news.trends country=india, monthly, mention match, 2024-06 – 2026-04 plotted. "Everything else" = all articles minus India-placed articles, so it includes the ~45% that are not placed anywhere. May 2026 dropped: the all-coverage count (589) is ingested, but India shows only 6 because geography labels stop at 2026-05-01. Plotting it would show a collapse that is really the labelling pipeline catching up. Peaks: Nov 2024 (India 1,744) and Dec 2025 (India 880), the stubble-burning and winter-inversion season.

6 · Studied vs reported vs patented — four separate lanes, never added

Src: research.geography (global_comparison, claim "air pollution"). Lanes: news = country an article is about; research authorship = the health literature index first-author affiliation; journal country = the health literature index publishing journal's country (not where the study was done); patents = assignee country. The tool reported no window for these lanes (the health literature index covers its full history; patents run to 2024). Its news lane counts India at 14,696, a different match from panel 2's 9,245, so the two are not interchangeable. India is not in the top 12 journal countries, so that bar is absent rather than zero. The largest patent bucket (1,502) has a blank assignee country.

Tool artefact: global_comparison's "focus" block returned India research = 0 and patents = 0, but its own lanes list India with 1,319 first-author papers and IN with 39 patents. The lane rows are used here and the focus block is ignored.

7 · The critical stories

Src: news.critical, priority-band ranked, match=central, 2025-06-01 – 2026-06-01 (exclusive). 12 requested, 7 returned, 3 ids unresolved in the article store, 2 rejected as duplicates or irrelevant. Headlines are shown as published (two are in Hindi).

8 · Data quality — trust the map for the right reasons

  • Placement: only 54.9% of matched articles carry a country, 50.2% a state and 47.0% a city (news.geography). Every map shows the placed half, not all coverage.
  • Share vs share: share_pct is a share of placements. Multi-country articles count once per country, so India's 31.2% of placements equals 59.3% of placed articles.
  • Windows: news counts run Jun 2024 – May 2026. Geography runs May 2024 – Apr 2026, bounded by the labelling pipeline. Ingest after June 2026 is 19%, 2% and 0.4% of a normal month (system.freshness), so nothing later is used. Typed research runs 2017–2025.
  • Three India numbers: 9,245 (news.geography, placed), 8,291 (news.trends country=india, Jun 2024 – May 2026) and 14,696 (global_comparison news lane, window unstated). These are different matches, not contradictions.
  • Artefacts: "centre" as a state (most likely the union government); "sirsa" (most likely the minister's surname); "congress", "earth", "winter" and "california" as cities; "punjab" ambiguous between India and Pakistan. Cameroon (671, lift 8.6×) is a high-lift row of the kind the tool's own caveat warns about. A collision with "Centre", which is also a Cameroonian region, is plausible but not verified. Iceland (277) may be the volcanic-eruption coverage.
  • Research series: the typed corpus shows 14,501 papers in 2018 against 4,462 in 2017 and 6,849 in 2019, which looks like an ingest artefact. The title-only series (analysis.history) rises steadily from 2,348 (2017) to 5,158 (2025).
  • Lift is coverage share for this term divided by that place's share of all news. A small place with a few articles can show a huge lift.
